This pronounced sexual dimorphism in body length is a common feature among lacertid lizards and is often linked to male-male competition for territories and access to gravid females. The species is typically found in arid, rocky habitats with sparse vegetation, where it forages actively during the warmer parts of the day. Its life history is shaped by the constraints of a short active season, which influences growth rates and reproductive scheduling.
